name: Mixed-type Autoimmune Hemolytic Anemia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: No standardized formal criteria; diagnosis based on clinical and laboratory findings

criteria.description: Positive direct antiglobulin (Coombs) test with both warm and cold autoantibodies detected
Laboratory evidence of hemolysis including elevated lactate dehydrogenase, indirect hyperbilirubinemia, and low haptoglobin
Presence of anemia with reticulocytosis and clinical signs consistent with hemolytic anemia
Exclusion of secondary causes such as lymphoproliferative disorders or infections

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of anemia with laboratory evidence of hemolysis plus positive direct antiglobulin test demonstrating both warm and cold autoantibodies
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of clinical, serological, and laboratory data; exclusion of secondary causes is important.

laboratory: Positive direct antiglobulin (Coombs) test for IgG and complement (C3d)
Peripheral blood smear showing spherocytes and red cell agglutination
genetic: No specific genetic mutations identified; may be associated with underlying autoimmune predisposition
other: Exclusion of secondary causes such as lymphoproliferative disorders or infections

distinguishingFeatures: Positive Coombs test primarily for warm IgG antibodies
Usually no acrocyanosis or cold-induced symptoms
Positive Coombs test primarily for complement (C3d) only
Cold-induced symptoms predominate without warm antibody involvement
Lack of spherocytosis on blood smear

redFlags: Rapidly progressive anemia with hemodynamic instability
Neurological deterioration secondary to severe anemia
references: Berentsen S, Barcellini W. Autoimmune hemolytic anemias. N Engl J Med. 2021;385(15):1407-1419.
Hill QA, Stamps R, Massey E, et al. The diagnosis and management of primary autoimmune haemolytic anaemia. Br J Haematol. 2017;176(3):395-411.
Orphanet: Mixed-type autoimmune hemolytic anemia. ORPHA:90036.
